SEA.head: A tough matchup for the Kraken

story.head: The Ducks come in rested
paras: The Kraken won the teams’ first meeting this season, 3-2 in Seattle on Nov 23. The Kraken (12-10-1) beat Edmonton 4-2 on Nov 27, while the Ducks (12-14-1) lost 5-3 to Los Angeles the same night. The Kraken played last night, and the Ducks are rested. This is a Pacific Division matchup, with the Kraken fourth (tied for 22nd in the NHL) and the Ducks fifth (tied for 22nd). The Pacific has been the weakest of the four divisions so far.

The Kraken’s record (.543) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.442), largely thanks to their finishing. The Ducks have played better than their record (.463) says: their chances are worth about .525, and losses in one-goal games have held them back.

The Kraken rarely threaten on the penalty kill (32nd) and ice the puck a lot (31st). They also give up a lot of shots (32nd), so the Ducks are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against them. As for the Ducks, they hit a lot (4th), give up a lot of dangerous shots (31st) and have had shaky goaltending (29th). Anaheim has allowed 3.70 goals a game, the fourth most in the league. Both teams like to play fast, so expect an open game.

Berkly Catton (8 G / 11 A / 19 P in 23 GP) leads the Kraken in scoring, and Kaapo Kakko (6 G / 11 A / 17 P in 23 GP) isn’t far behind. For the Ducks, Cutter Gauthier (23 G / 9 A / 32 P in 26 GP) leads the way in scoring, with five goals in eight games against Seattle since 2023-24. Mikael Granlund (8 G / 23 A / 31 P in 26 GP) isn’t far behind.

Joey Daccord (6-5-0 / .881 SV% in 11 GS) will likely start for Seattle. Anaheim has two options in net: Laurent Brossoit (5-2-0 / .876 SV% in 7 GS) and Lukáš Dostál (4-7-1 / .857 SV% in 13 GS). Brossoit has started four of their last ten games, including the last one on Nov 27. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
